title: Find the Integer Added to Array II
summary: Given two integer arrays, nums1 and nums2, find the smallest integer x such that removing any two elements from nums1 and adding x to the remaining elements (or subtracting x if it is negative) results in nums2.
statement: Given two integer arrays, nums1 and nums2, find the smallest integer x such that removing any two elements from nums1 and adding x to the remaining elements (or subtracting x if it is negative) results in nums2. The two arrays must contain the same integers with the same frequencies.
constraints: nums1 has exactly two more integer elements than nums2.
Remove exactly two nums1 indices, then add the same integer x to every remaining value so its multiset equals nums2.
At least one solution exists; return the smallest possible x.
hints: After sorting, nums2’s smallest value must align with one of nums1’s first three values because only two nums1 values are removed.
Try those three offsets and greedily skip at most two mismatches with two pointers.
For candidate i=0,1,2 set x=nums2[0]-nums1[i]; scan sorted arrays, matching shifted values and counting skips; minimize valid x.
Every solution exposes its first kept nums1 value among the first three, and sorted matching uniquely determines whether that offset can delete only two values.
editorial: Every solution exposes its first kept nums1 value among the first three, and sorted matching uniquely determines whether that offset can delete only two values.

tests.explanation: Remove four and eight; adding negative two to [20,16,12] produces [18,14,10], exactly the target multiset.
Remove both threes and add two to the two fives, producing [7,7].
